data.content_ref: inline:The target triggers its own defeating countercondition. Countercondition 1 stipulates that if verisimilitude (truth-likeness) is required to justify action, the argument fails because Tichý and Miller showed Popper's formal verisimilitude is incoherent. Yet the target's own mechanism concedes that acting on a theory requires treating the unrefuted as 'provisionally reliable' — a property that is inherently truth-related (reliability tracks how well a theory approximates reality in its predictions). 'Provisionally reliable' cannot be grounded in testability alone, because a highly testable theory that has survived falsification could still be radically false in untested domains; only verisimilitude or a truth-likeness proxy could bridge 'survived testing' to 'reliable for action.' By the target's own logic, once action requires a truth-proxy and the only formal candidate (verisimilitude) is incoherent, the defense collapses. The target never identifies any alternative truth-likeness measure that survives the Tichý/Miller objection, so its admission that action demands 'provisional reliability' activates countercondition 1 and the argument defeats itself.
